topics.title: Given one trigonometric function, find another

questions.hint: sec is negative in Quadrant II within the given range.
questions.solution: Since \(\sec \theta < 0\) and \(0^{\circ} \le \theta \le 180^{\circ}\), \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant II. In Quadrant II, tangent is negative. \(\cos \theta = -\frac{5}{13} \implies \sin \theta = \frac{12}{13}\). Thus, \(\tan \theta = -\frac{12}{5}\).

steps.work:
\(0^{\circ} \le \theta \le 180^{\circ}\) (Q1 or Q2) and \(\sec \theta = -\frac{13}{5} < 0\).
Secant is negative in **Quadrant II**.
In Q2, tangent is negative.

Visualizing the value: A right-angled reference triangle can be formed in this quadrant to find the exact ratios.

steps.explain: Calculate the required ratio using a right-angled triangle.
steps.work: 1. Analyze given ratio: \[ |\\text{secant}| = \frac{13}{5} \\implies \text{hyp}=13, \text{adj}=5 \] 2. Use Pythagoras Theorem: \[ \text{opp} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12 \] 3. Calculate final ratio: \[ \tan \theta = -\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}} = -\frac{12}{5} \]

questions.stem: If \(\csc B = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(\cos B < 0\), find \(\tan B\).
questions.hint: Positive cosecant (sine) and negative cosine means Quadrant II.
questions.solution: In Quadrant II, tangent is negative. Since \(\sin B = \frac{2}{5}\), \(\cos B = -\sqrt{1 - (2/5)^2} = -\frac{\sqrt{21}}{5}\). Thus, \(\tan B = \frac{\sin B}{\cos B} = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{21}}\).

steps.work:
\(\csc B = \frac{5}{2} > 0\) means Q1 or Q2.
\(\cos B < 0\) means Q2 or Q3.
Both conditions are met only in **Quadrant II**.
In Q2, tangent is negative.

Visualizing the value: A right-angled reference triangle can be formed in this quadrant to find the exact ratios.

steps.explain: Calculate the required ratio using a right-angled triangle.
steps.work: 1. Analyze given ratio: \[ |\\text{cosecant}| = \frac{5}{2} \\implies \text{hyp}=5, \text{opp}=2 \] 2. Use Pythagoras Theorem: \[ \text{adj} = \sqrt{5^2 - 2^2} = \sqrt{21} \] 3. Calculate final ratio: \[ \tan B = -\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}} = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{21}} \]

questions.hint: Negative secant (cosine) and negative cosecant (sine) means Quadrant III.
questions.solution: In Quadrant III, cotangent is positive. \(\cos \theta = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). \(\sin \theta = -\sqrt{1 - \cos^2 \theta} = -\sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{3}} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\). Thus, \(\cot \theta = \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \frac{-1/\sqrt{3}}{-\sqrt{2}/\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

steps.work:
\(\sec \theta = -\sqrt{3} < 0\) means Q2 or Q3.
\(\csc \theta < 0\) means Q3 or Q4.
Both conditions are met only in **Quadrant III**.
In Q3, cotangent is positive.

Visualizing the value: A right-angled reference triangle can be formed in this quadrant to find the exact ratios.

steps.explain: Calculate the required ratio using a right-angled triangle.
steps.work: 1. Analyze given ratio: \[ |\\text{secant}| = \sqrt{3} \\implies \text{hyp}=\sqrt{3}, \text{adj}=1 \] 2. Use Pythagoras Theorem: \[ \text{opp} = \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 - 1^2} = \sqrt{2} \] 3. Calculate final ratio: \[ \cot \theta = \frac{\text{adj}}{\text{opp}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \]
